The energy  

\[
E = 3.9\times10^{-6}\ \text{eV}
\]

corresponds to a frequency  

\[
\nu = \frac{E}{h}= \frac{3.9\times10^{-6}\,\text{eV}\times1.602\times10^{-19}\,\text{J/eV}}{6.626\times10^{-34}\,\text{J·s}}
      \approx 9.4\times10^{8}\ \text{Hz}\;(0.94\ \text{GHz}),
\]

i.e. a wavelength of about 31 cm.  

The only well‑known astrophysical line near this frequency is the **hyperfine 21‑cm line of neutral hydrogen**, whose rest frequency is 1.420 GHz. The observed line at 0.94 GHz is therefore the 21‑cm line red‑shifted by  

\[
z = \frac{\nu_{\rm rest}}{\nu_{\rm obs}}-1 \approx \frac{1.420}{0.94}-1 \approx 0.5,
\]

consistent with a source at a distance of ~2 Gpc.

In the Milky Way, the 21‑cm line is seen in **absorption** primarily from the **cold neutral atomic medium (CNM)**, because the cold HI clouds have low spin temperatures and can absorb background radio continuum.

Thus the absorption line would most likely be associated with the cold atomic interstellar medium.

**Answer: C**.
